parsed.explanation: Thin trans-specific record, so I extrapolate from structural signals. A criminal statute (Art. 354, 3 months to 2 years) reaches a trans visitor whose conduct or partner is read as same-sex. The 2013 wedding arrests, bar closure and fines show enforcement, though pre-code and not trans-specific. Police refuse to investigate crimes against LGBTQ+ people, and no general anti-discrimination protection exists, so recourse is thin. Official rhetoric is hostile and social attitudes are hostile, with healthcare discrimination documented. There is no documented facility, border or custody rule for trans visitors, and no documented trans-specific violence. The uncorroborated imprisonment claim and the unreliable survey are excluded. No legal gender recognition and no marker-change route are resident gaps, weighted lightly. Overall: Elevated-to-High risk, driven by criminalisation with no working remedy in a hostile climate.
